info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Generated from the live router — every operation below is a route the unified cloud binary actually serves. Tagged by product: the first path segment after /v1/.

get.summary: listLBs lists the load balancers the caller's org owns, under their friendly names.
get.description:
listLBs lists the load balancers the caller's org owns, under their friendly names.
The account-wide DigitalOcean inventory is filtered to the caller's org prefix, so
another tenant's load balancers are invisible rather than forbidden.

post.summary: createLB creates a load balancer in the caller's org under a friendly name.
post.description:
createLB creates a load balancer in the caller's org under a friendly name. Name
and region are required; omitted forwarding rules default to plain HTTP 80→80, so
a minimal create still yields a usable load balancer, and a name already taken in
this org is a 409.

delete.summary: deleteLB deletes one load balancer the caller's org owns.
delete.description:
deleteLB deletes one load balancer the caller's org owns. Ownership is confirmed
before the delete, so a cross-tenant id is a not-found rather than another org's loss.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean load balancer id from the path.

get.summary: getLB reads one load balancer the caller's org owns.
get.description:
getLB reads one load balancer the caller's org owns. A load balancer in another
org's namespace is reported not-found, never forbidden.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean load balancer id from the path.

get.summary: listVPCs lists the VPCs owned by the caller's org, under their friendly names.
get.description:
listVPCs lists the VPCs owned by the caller's org, under their friendly names.
The account-wide DigitalOcean inventory is filtered to the caller's org prefix,
so another tenant's VPCs are invisible rather than forbidden.

post.summary: createVPC creates a VPC in the caller's org under a friendly name.
post.description:
createVPC creates a VPC in the caller's org under a friendly name.
Name and region are required; an empty ip_range lets DigitalOcean pick the CIDR.
A name already taken in this org is a 409.

delete.summary: deleteVPC deletes one VPC the caller's org owns.
delete.description:
deleteVPC deletes one VPC the caller's org owns. Ownership is confirmed before
the delete, so a cross-tenant id is a not-found rather than another org's loss.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean VPC id from the path.

get.summary: getVPC reads one VPC the caller's org owns.
get.description:
getVPC reads one VPC the caller's org owns. A VPC in another org's namespace is
reported not-found, never forbidden, so the id space leaks no existence.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean VPC id from the path.

forwarding_rules.description: ForwardingRules are the entry→target port mappings; empty defaults to HTTP 80→80.

name.description:
Name is the friendly load balancer name, a DNS-safe slug of at most 40
characters. It is namespaced to the caller's org before it reaches DigitalOcean.

region.description: Region is the DigitalOcean region slug to create the load balancer in. Required.

size.description: Size is DO's size slug; empty takes DO's default.

type.description: Type is DO's load balancer type; empty takes DO's default (REGIONAL).

ip_range.description: IPRange is the VPC's CIDR; empty lets DigitalOcean assign one.

name.description:
Name is the friendly VPC name, a DNS-safe slug of at most 40 characters.
It is namespaced to the caller's org before it reaches DigitalOcean.

region.description: Region is the DigitalOcean region slug to create the VPC in. Required.

entry_port.description: EntryPort is the port the load balancer listens on.

entry_protocol.description: EntryProtocol is the protocol the load balancer listens with, e.g. http or https.

target_port.description: TargetPort is the port on the backend droplets.

target_protocol.description: TargetProtocol is the protocol used to reach the backend droplets.

loadBalancers.description: LoadBalancers are the caller's own load balancers; another org's are invisible.

id.description: ID is DigitalOcean's own load balancer id — the value GET and DELETE address.

ip.description: IP is the load balancer's public address, empty while it is still provisioning.

name.description: Name is the FRIENDLY name the tenant supplied, with the org prefix stripped.

status.description: Status is DO's own lifecycle value, e.g. new or active.

targets.description: Targets is the count of backend droplets attached to the load balancer.

type.description: Type is DO's load balancer type, e.g. REGIONAL or GLOBAL.

vpcs.description: VPCs are the caller's own VPCs; another org's are invisible, not forbidden.

cidr.description: CIDR is the VPC's IP range in CIDR notation.

id.description: ID is DigitalOcean's own VPC id — the value GET and DELETE address.

name.description: Name is the FRIENDLY name the tenant supplied, with the org prefix stripped.

region.description: Region is the DigitalOcean region slug the VPC lives in.

status.description: Status is always "active" — DO VPCs have no lifecycle state.

subnets.description:
Subnets is always empty: a DO VPC is a single IP range with no sub-network
objects in the API.
